correctness.rationale: Torus averaging over full monomial stabilizer including finite components shows the unrestricted total-degree multipliers reduce exactly to polynomials P(u) of degree ≤K. Orthogonal monomial powers yield exact moment constraints R(1)=1,R^(j)(1)=0 (1≤j<r) for R=1−(1−u)^rP(u) and E=(G_(K+r)^−1)_(00). All moment weights are positive. Stirling with norm normalization gives w_k=Ck(1+O(k^−1)), uniformly only in k for fixed parameters, hence C G00=log(K+r)+Λ+o(1). Rescaled off-diagonal moment blocks converge to positive-definite H_ij=1/(i+j), b_i=1/i. Exact Cauchy determinant yields bᵀH^−1b=2H_(r−1). Schur complement proves C/E=logK+Λ−2H_(r−1)+o(1); subtract and invert for error difference. Independent exact Fraction linear algebra verified r=2..11, 5 unrelated critical weight tails at k=50000 approached Ck, and the n=m=a=r? simple Dirichlet reciprocal difference approached −2 for r=2. Finite tests do not prove all parameters or limits.

value.rationale: A genuinely natural critical boundary-zero approximation invariant: all fixed multiplicities have the *same* leading squared error C/logK, so the explicit universal 2CH_(r−1)/(logK)^2 is the first order distinguishing singularity multiplicity. The r-dependence is a mathematically motivated sharp structural constant, independent of dimension and exponent distribution after correct normalization. It is not merely another single-instance table computation, a trivial renaming, or an asserted large general theorem. It can serve as precise quantitative benchmark in Dirichlet cyclic approximation.

final_claim: For fixed n≥m≥1, positive integer exponents a_j, d=Σa_j, normalized monomial u=c∏z_j^a_j (c²=d^d/∏a_j^a_j) in the n-ball, critical Dirichlet coefficient exponent α*=n−(m−1)/2, and any fixed r≥1, unrestricted squared error E_K,r=min_{deg q≤dK}||1−(1−u)^r q||² satisfies C/E_K,r=logK+Λ−2H_(r−1)+o(1), C=(n−1)!(2π)^((m−1)/2) sqrt(∏a_j)d^(1−m/2). Therefore lim_K C(E_K,r^−1−E_K,1^−1)=−2H_(r−1) and lim_K (logK)^2(E_K,r−E_K,1)=2C H_(r−1).
